title: The Expansion of the Maratha Power

facts.text: After the death of Emperor Aurangzeb, Prince Azamshah, who was in the South, marched towards Delhi to seize the imperial throne.
facts.quote: After the death of Emperor Aurangzeb, there ensued a struggle among his sons for the throne of Delhi. Prince Azamshah was in the South. At once, he marched towards Delhi to seize the imperial throne.

facts.text: Azamshah released Shahu Maharaj, believing a conflict between him and Maharani Tarabai for the gadi would sap Maratha strength.
facts.quote: Azamshah believed that if Shahu Maharaj was released, there would arise a conflict between him and Maharani Tarabai for the gadi of the Maratha Chhatrapati. Azamshah felt that this would sap the Maratha strength and therefore, released Shahu Maharaj.

facts.text: The armies of Shahu Maharaj and Maharani Tarabai fought a battle at Khed on the bank of the Bheema; Shahu Maharaj won.
facts.quote: The armies of Shahu Maharaj and Maharani Tarabai fought a battle at Khed on the bank of the Bheema. Shahu Maharaj won the battle.

facts.text: Shahu Maharaj captured Satara and got himself crowned; Satara became the capital of the Maratha kingdom.
facts.quote: He captured Satara. He got himself crowned. Satara became the capital of the Maratha kingdom.

facts.text: Maharani Tarabai proclaimed her minor son Shivaji II as the Chhatrapati at Pahnala in 1710 CE.
facts.quote: Maharani Tarabai proclaimed her minor son Shivaji II as the Chhatrapati at Pahnala in 1710 CE.

facts.text: This gave rise to an independent Maratha Kingdom at Kolhapur besides the one at Satara.
facts.quote: This gave rise to an indendepent Maratha Kingdom at Kolhapur besides the one at Satara.

facts.text: The early part of Shahu Maharaj's life was spent in Mughal camps, so he knew Mughal politics from close quarters.
facts.quote: The early part of Shahu Maharaj's life was spent in Mughal camps. So, he had seen Mughal politics from close quarters.

facts.text: The Marathas adopted a new policy: instead of fighting the Mughal power, they would protect it and expand their own empire in that role.
facts.quote: Instead of fighting with the Mughal power, they decided to protect it and expand their own empire in that role. They believed that restoring an old temple is as good as building a new one.

facts.text: The Mughal power faced Irani and Afghani invaders from the north-west and local Pathan, Rajput, Jat and Rohila rulers, so the Delhi Court needed the help of the Marathas.
facts.quote: The Mughal power faced the threat of the Irani and Afghani invaders from the north-west and also of the local Pathan, local Rajput, Jat and Rohilas rulers. ... Due to all these the Delhi Court needed the help of the Marathas.

facts.text: After his release, Shahu Maharaj made Balaji Vishwanath a Peshwa.
facts.quote: After Shahu Maharaj was released by the Mughals, he made Balaji Vishwanath, a Peshwa.

facts.text: Balaji Vishwanath hailed from Shrivardhan, in Konkan.
facts.quote: Balaji hailed from Shrivardhan, in Konkan.

facts.text: Kanhoji Angre, the chief of the Maratha Navy, sided with Maharani Tarabai and attacked the territories of Shahu Maharaj.
facts.quote: Kanhoji Angre was the chief of Maratha Navy. He chose to side with Maharani Tarabai and attacked the territories of Shahu Maharaj.

facts.text: Balaji avoided war and won Kanhoji Angre over to Shahu Maharaj's side.
facts.quote: Balaji avoided the war and won Kanhoji over to Shahu Maharaj's side.

facts.text: The Sayyid brothers, Abdulla (Hasan) and Hussein Ali, had become very influential in the Delhi court.
facts.quote: The Sayyid brothers, Abdulla (Hasan) and Hussein Ali had become very influential.

facts.text: In 1719 CE, with the help of the Sayyid brothers, Balaji obtained sanads to collect chauthai and sardeshmukhi from the Mughal territory in the Deccan.
facts.quote: With their help, in 1719 CE Balaji obtained from the Mughal Emperor, the grants or sanads to collect chauthai and sardeshmukhi from the Mughal territory in the Deccan.

facts.text: Chauthai was the right to collect one fourth part of the revenue.
facts.quote: one fourth part (chauthai)

facts.text: Sardeshmukhi was the right to collect one tenth part of the revenue.
facts.quote: one tenth part (sardeshmukhi) of the revenue from the Mughal territory in the Deccan

facts.text: After the death of Balaji Vishwanath, Shahu Maharaj appointed Balaji's son Bajirao I the Peshwa in 1720 CE.
facts.quote: After the death of Balaji Vishwanath, Shahu Maharaj appointed Balaji's son, Bajirao I the Peshwa in 1720 CE.

facts.text: Bajirao I expanded the Maratha Empire during his term of 20 years.
facts.quote: He expanded the Maratha Empire during his term of 20 years.

facts.text: The Mughal emperor Farukhsear appointed Nizam-ul-Mulk the Subhedar of Deccan.
facts.quote: The Mughal emperor Farukhsear appointed Nizam-ul-Mulk the Subhedar of Deccan.

facts.text: In 1713 CE the Nizam tried to establish his separate existence at Hyderabad.
facts.quote: In 1713 CE Nizam tried to establish his separate existence at Hyderabad.

facts.text: The Nizam was against the Maratha Chauthai-Sardeshmukhi rights and captured some part of the Pune Pargana.
facts.quote: Nizam was against it. He captured some part of the Pune Pargana.

facts.text: Bajirao defeated the Nizam at Palkhed near Aurangabad; the Nizam accepted the Maratha right to collect Chauthai-Sardeshmukhi.
facts.quote: He defeated the Nizam at Palkhed near Aurangabad. The Nizam accepted the Maratha right to collect Chauthai-Sardeshmukhi.

facts.text: Bajirao sent Malharrao Holkar, Ranoji Shinde and Udaji Pawar to Malwa under the leadership of his brother Chimajiappa.
facts.quote: Bajirao sent Malharrao Holkar, Ranoji Shinde and Udaji Pawar under the leadership of his brother Chimajiappa to Malwa.

facts.text: Malwa, in today's Madhya Pradesh, was part of the Mughal empire.
facts.quote: Malwa in todays Madhya Pradesh was part of the Mughal empire.

facts.text: Bundelkhand means some part of today's Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh: areas around Jhansi, Panna and Sagar.
facts.quote: Bundelkhand means some part of today's Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh - areas around Jhansi, Panna and Sagar.

facts.text: King Chhatrasal of Bundelkhand was defeated by Mohmmad Khan Bangush, the Mughal Subhedar of Allahabad, and appealed to Bajirao for help.
facts.quote: King Chhatrasal had established his own kingdom in Bundelkhand. The Mughal Subhedar Mohmmad Khan Bangush of Allahabad attacked Bundelkhand and had defeated Chhatrasal. Chhatrasal appealed to Bajirao for help.

facts.text: Bajirao defeated Bangush and Chhatrasal honoured Bajirao; the Marathas established supremacy in Malwa and Bundelkhand.
facts.quote: He defeated Bangush. Chhatrasal honoured Bajirao. This is how Marathas established their supremacy in Malwa and Bundelkhand.

facts.text: When the Emperor declined to make him Subhedar of Malwa, Bajirao marched on Delhi in 1737 CE and took the Mughals by surprise.
facts.quote: As the Emperor declined this demand, Bajirao marched on Delhi in 1737 CE. The Mughals were taken by surprise.

facts.text: In a letter, Chhatrasal compared himself to the elephant whose leg is caught by the crocodile and said only Bajirao could save him.
facts.quote: My situation is like the elephant whose leg is caught by the crocodile. You are the only one who can save me.

facts.text: Bajirao defeated the Nizam at Bhopal; the Nizam agreed to secure the sanad of Malwa subhedari for the Marathas.
facts.quote: Bajirao defeated him at Bhopal. Nizam agreed to secure the sanad of Malwa subhedari for the Marathas from the Badshah.

facts.text: Vasai and Thane on the Konkan coast were in the possession of the Portuguese; Chimaji conquered Thane and the adjacent areas.
facts.quote: The territories of Vasai and Thane on the Konkan coast were in the possession of the Portuguese. ... Chimaji conquered Thane and the adjacent areas.

facts.text: In 1739 CE Chimaji laid siege to the Vasai fort and forced the Portuguese to surrender.
facts.quote: In 1739 CE, he laid siege to the Vasai fort. ... Chimaji continued the siege with perseverance and forced the Portuguese to surrender.

facts.text: Nadirshah, the Emperor of Iran, invaded India; by the time Bajirao reached Burhanpur, Nadirshah had returned to Iran with booty looted from Delhi.
facts.quote: Nadirshah, the Emperor of Iran, invaded India. ... By the time he reached Burhanpur, Nadirshah had returned to Iran with an enormous booty looted from Delhi.

facts.text: In April 1740 Bajirao breathed his last at Raverkhedi on the banks of the Narmada.
facts.quote: In April 1740, Bajirao breathed his last at Raverkhedi on the banks of the Narmada.

facts.text: In Bajirao's time the Shinde, Holkar, Pawar and Gaikwad families attained prominence.
facts.quote: In his time, the Shinde, Holkar, Pawar, Gaikwad families attained prominence.
